title: Flux Dotfiles Manager Configuration
description: Schema for Flux dotfiles manager configuration file (config.toml)

repo_path.description: Repository path where dotfiles are stored. Supports tilde expansion (~).

docs.main:
Repository path where dotfiles are stored.

Supports tilde expansion (`~`) which will be expanded to your home directory.

**Examples:**
- `~/.dotfiles` - Standard location in home directory
- `/home/user/dotfiles` - Absolute path
- `~/Documents/dotfiles` - Custom location with tilde expansion

backup_dir.description: Directory for backups (created automatically on conflicts). Supports tilde expansion (~).

docs.main:
Directory for backups created automatically when conflicts occur.

Supports tilde expansion (`~`). Backups are created when:
- Installing files that would overwrite existing files
- Switching profiles with conflicting configurations

**Examples:**
- `~/.dotfiles-backup` - Default backup location
- `/tmp/dotfiles-backups` - Temporary backup location

current_profile.description: Current active profile name. Must be alphanumeric with underscores or hyphens.

docs.main:
Current active profile name.

Profiles allow you to have different configurations for different environments (work, home, laptop, etc.). Files can be marked as profile-specific in the `tools` section.

**Constraints:**
- Must be alphanumeric with underscores or hyphens
- Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`

**Examples:**
- `default` - Default profile
- `work` - Work environment
- `laptop` - Laptop-specific configuration

Symlink resolution strategy for managing dotfiles.

- **auto**: Use relative if possible, absolute if needed (recommended)
- **relative**: Always create relative symlinks
- **absolute**: Always create absolute symlinks
- **follow**: Follow existing symlinks, replace target
- **replace**: Replace symlinks with actual files (copy)
enumValues: Use relative if possible, absolute if needed (recommended)
docs.defaultValue: Use relative if possible, absolute if needed (recommended)

default_remote.description: Default remote name for git push operations (optional, defaults to 'origin')

default_branch.description: Default branch name for git push operations (optional, defaults to 'main' if no HEAD)

include.description: List of config files to include and merge. Later files override earlier ones. Paths can be relative (to config file directory), absolute, or use tilde expansion.

tools.description: Tool configurations. Each key is a tool name, and each value contains files to track.

docs.main:
Tool configurations for managing dotfiles.

Each key is a tool name (e.g., `sway`, `cursor`, `vim`), and each value contains a list of files to track. Files can be profile-specific by adding a `profile` field.

**Example:**
```toml
[tools.sway]
files = [
    { repo = "config", dest = ".config/sway/config" },
    { repo = "config.work", dest = ".config/sway/config", profile = "work" }
]
```

files.description: List of files to track for this tool

repo.description: Path to file in repository (relative to tool directory in repo)

docs.main:
Path to file in repository, relative to the tool's directory.

For example, if the tool is `sway` and `repo = "config"`, the file will be at `{repo_path}/sway/config`.

dest.description: Destination path in home directory (relative to home, e.g., '.config/sway/config'). Supports simple templates like `{{profile}}`, `{{host}}`, `{{user}}`.

docs.main:
Destination path in home directory.

This is relative to your home directory. Use dot notation for hidden files/directories.

You can also use simple template variables which will be expanded at runtime:
- `{{profile}}` - current profile name
- `{{host}}` - hostname
- `{{user}}` / `{{username}}` - current user
- `{{os}}` - operating system identifier
- custom variables from `[environment.values]`.

**Examples:**
- `.config/sway/config` - Standard config location
- `.vimrc` - Vim configuration
- `.bashrc` - Bash configuration
- `.config/{{profile}}/sway/config` - Profile-specific path

profile.description: Optional profile name. If specified, this file is only active for this profile.

docs.main:
Optional profile name.

If specified, this file will only be active when the `current_profile` matches this value. This allows you to have different configurations for different environments.

**Example:**
```toml
{ repo = "config.work", dest = ".config/sway/config", profile = "work" }
```

This file will only be used when `current_profile = "work"`.

conditions.description: Optional conditions that control when this entry is active (OS, host, env vars, available commands). All specified conditions must match.

os.description: List of operating systems where this entry applies (e.g., "linux", "darwin"). If omitted, matches all OSes.

host.description: List of hostnames where this entry applies. If omitted, matches all hosts.

env.description: Required environment variable values. Each key/value pair must match the current environment.

cmd_exists.description: Commands that must exist in PATH for this entry to apply.

secret.description: Mark this entry as secret. Secret entries are treated with stricter permissions and should not have their contents displayed in logs/diffs.

secret_key.description: Logical secret key or handle used by the configured backend (for example, an environment variable name when using the "env" backend).

packages.description: Package declarations for declarative package management. Each key is a package name.

docs.main:
Package declarations for declarative package management.

Each key is a package name, and the value specifies version constraints and optional metadata. This allows you to declare which packages should be installed and their versions.

**Example:**
```toml
[packages.git]
version = "latest"
description = "Version control system"

[packages.vim]
version = "~9.0"
min_version = "9.0.0"
```

name.description: Package name (optional, key name is used if not specified)

docs.main:
Version constraint for the package.

**Supported formats:**
- `latest` - Install the latest available version
- `1.9.0` - Exact version
- `~1.9` - Compatible version (>= 1.9.0, < 2.0.0)
- `>=2.0` - Minimum version
- `<3.0` - Maximum version (use `max_version` instead)

**Examples:**
- `latest` - Always use latest
- `1.9.0` - Pin to specific version
- `~1.9` - Compatible with 1.9.x

services.description: Service declarations for declarative service management. Each key is a service name.

docs.main:
Service declarations for declarative service management.

Each key is a service name, and the value specifies whether the service should be enabled, running, and/or autostarted. This allows you to manage systemd services declaratively.

**Example:**
```toml
[services.ssh]
enabled = true
running = true
package = "openssh-server"

[services.docker]
enabled = true
autostart = true
```

name.description: Service name (optional, key name is used if not specified)

docs.main:
Whether the service should be enabled to start at boot.

When `true`, the service will be enabled in systemd (systemctl enable).
docs.defaultValue: Service will not be enabled at boot

running.description: Should be running now (optional, if not specified, follows enabled state)

autostart.description: Autostart on user login (for user services)

docs.main:
Whether the service should autostart on user login.

This is typically used for user services (systemd --user). When `true`, the service will be configured to start automatically when the user logs in.
docs.defaultValue: Service will not autostart on login

docs.main:
Environment configuration for setting environment variables and shell preferences.

This section allows you to declare environment variables and shell settings that should be applied to your system.

**Example:**
```toml
[environment]
variables = { EDITOR = "nvim", SHELL = "/bin/bash" }
shell = "/bin/zsh"
```

values.description: Template variables for use in repo/dest paths and other strings. These are merged with built-in variables like `user`, `home`, `host`, `os`, and `profile`.

hooks.description: Hooks configuration for executing commands at various points in the apply/commit lifecycle

pre_apply.description: Commands to run before applying changes. If any command fails, the apply is aborted.

post_apply.description: Commands to run after applying changes. Failures are non-fatal (warnings only).

pre_commit.description: Commands to run before committing changes. If any command fails, the commit is aborted.

post_commit.description: Commands to run after committing changes. Failures are non-fatal (warnings only).

conditionSpec.description: Conditions that control when a config entry should be active. All specified condition groups must match.

os.description: List of operating systems where this entry applies (e.g., "linux", "darwin"). If omitted, matches all OSes.

host.description: List of hostnames where this entry applies. If omitted, matches all hosts.

env.description: Required environment variable values. All specified variables must match.

cmd_exists.description: List of commands that must exist in PATH. If omitted, no command checks are performed.
